name: Design Experiments
description: Make a prediction, change something deliberately, and learn from a playtest.

cards.title: Change one thing
cards.task: Choose one measurable parameter. Play the baseline and write down what you expect. Keep everything else fixed, test a new value, and compare the two versions.
cards.reflection: What changed for the player? Did the result match your prediction?

cards.title: Find the tipping point
cards.task: Change one parameter in small steps until a previously successful strategy stops working. Record the last working value and the first failing value.
cards.reflection: What caused the strategy to break? Could another player still succeed?

cards.title: Go to the extremes
cards.task: Give one parameter its smallest and largest meaningful values. Play both versions before choosing an intermediate value.
cards.reflection: When does this parameter stop creating a challenge, and when does it block progress?

cards.title: Prediction duel
cards.task: Show two versions of the same encounter to a partner. Each person predicts which is harder and names the player skill being challenged. Test both.
cards.reflection: Where did your predictions disagree, and what evidence helped resolve it?

cards.title: What is doing the work?
cards.task: Remove one ingredient from an encounter, keeping the rest unchanged. Play before and after the removal.
cards.reflection: Which decision or challenge disappeared? Was the ingredient essential?

cards.title: Double it. Halve it.
cards.task: Choose a numeric parameter such as light radius or a resource allowance. Test roughly double and half its starting value, within meaningful limits.
cards.reflection: Did twice the value mean twice the challenge? Why might the relationship be uneven?

cards.title: Stay silent
cards.task: Let a new player try your scenario without explanations. Record one hesitation, one unexpected action, and one correctly understood rule on post-its.
cards.reflection: What did the player infer from the design, and what required explanation?

cards.title: Name the skill
cards.task: Choose one encounter and name the player skill you intend to test. Change one parameter to increase that demand. Ask a tester which skill they actually used.
cards.reflection: Did you test the intended skill, or did the player solve the problem another way?

cards.title: Help or hazard?
cards.task: Choose one spatial parameter. Test a larger range on a helpful ingredient, then on a threatening ingredient. Keep a separate baseline for each test.
cards.reflection: Why can the same direction of change make one situation easier and another harder?

cards.title: Try it twice
cards.task: Have the same player repeat an unchanged scenario. Record retries and their perceived difficulty after each attempt.
cards.reflection: What improved through learning even though no parameter changed?

cards.title: Strip away the story
cards.task: Recreate a small encounter with abstract markers and the same rules. Ask another group to explain its decisions before revealing the original fiction.
cards.reflection: Which parts of the challenge came from the system, and which clues came from its presentation?

cards.title: One plus one
cards.task: Test ingredient A alone, ingredient B alone, then both together. Keep their individual values unchanged and note the available strategies in each case.
cards.reflection: Did the combination create a new decision or simply more of the same demand?
